newsitem.title: UK: UK M4 tips scales further in favour of rate rise.
newsitem.headline: UK M4 tips scales further in favour of rate rise.

text.p: A sharp acceleration in UK broad money in August adds to the list of data showing strong economic growth and potential inflationary pressures, playing into the hands of the Bank of England which wants higher interest rates.

"M4 remains strong in August. It has again pushed above the monitoring range and is reflecting a possible danger to inflation. The next move in rates is likely to be up, not down," said Philip Shaw, group economist at Union Plc.
M4 grew 9.4 percent in the year to August compared with 9.0 percent in the year to July.
Several special factors were at work during the month, but analysts said they broadly offset one another.

The Treasury focused on the 900 million stg boost to M4 prompted by the merger of National & Provincial building society with Abbey National Plc. That was completed in August and led to special payouts to N&P savers and mortgage holders.
"That is equivalent to around 0.1 percent on M4 growth in the year," said Shaw.
But the fall in gilt repos included in M4 during the month partially offset this.
"A fall in gilt repo was a key factor and helped to disguise strong personal sector borrowing," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at BankAmerica.
In August, gilt repos fell by 400 million stg to 8.6 billion stg and reverse repos fell by 1.2 billion stg to 13.5 billion.
The figures will prove unhelpful to Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke if he is seeking to cut rates in the run-up to the general election, which must be held by May 1997.
And they will strengthen the hand of the Bank of England which wants to see base rates back up at 6.0 percent from their current level of 5.75 percent.
"They play into the hands of the governor and add to the great majority of evidence in the past few weeks suggesting the economy is picking up strongly," said Shaw.
The data shows the flourishing consumer sector is driving growth upward. Latest figures showed retail sales in August running at levels last seen in the 1980s consumer boom.

A breakdown of the M4 lending figures by the British Bankers' Association showed consumer credit continued to grow strongly in August. It was up 453 million stg in the month, down slightly from July's massive rise of 556 million stg, but still above the recently monthly average rise of 405 million stg.
Building Society Association figures covering the same month showed demand for mortgages remained strong in August, reinforcing growing evidence of a revival in the housing market.
Net new approvals fell slightly in August to 3.643 billion stg from 3.781 billion in August.
Adrian Coles, BSA's director-general, said the latest figures represented good news for the housing market.

"These figures provide the clearest indication that the housing market is returning to health, with the stronger-than- expected levels of lending over the summer period pointing to further improvements for the rest of the year."
